reckons.claim: There's stacks of robot hype and doom in the extremes. We think it'll land somewhere in the middle. Because it usually does.

research.quote: A hundred million people had given it a go by Tuesday.
research.source: Time, reporting a UBS analysis: ChatGPT reached 100 million users about two months after launch, the fastest-growing consumer app on record. The Tuesday is ours.

reckons.claim: This is a lot of years in a little chapter so we've pulled the bits that click together best. History was messier than this.

research.quote: Alan Turing, the code-cracking guy, famously imagined machines that could think like humans about halfway through last century.
research.source: Turing's 1950 paper “Computing Machinery and Intelligence”, in the journal Mind.

research.quote: Lovelace imagined a way to turn music into math so machines “might compose elaborate and scientific pieces of music of any degree of complexity”.
research.source: Ada Lovelace's notes on the Analytical Engine, 1843. The quoted words are hers, from Note A.

research.quote: In 1956, a summer camp in Dartmouth nudged the idea along. Ten guys, two months, one big idea: let's get in a room and crack intelligence.
research.source: The 1955 proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, which asked for “a 2 month, 10 man study”.

research.quote: But the first ones were built in Denver, in 1952.
research.source: The Utah Department of Transportation on the history of traffic signals: Denver installed the first electronically actuated system in 1952.

research.quote: It lost its first match against Kasparov, the Russian Grandmaster. But with a year's worth of tweaking, the computer won and the world freaked out.
research.source: IBM's own history of Deep Blue: lost to Kasparov in 1996, won the rematch in May 1997.

research.quote: IBM's Deep Blue was about the size of a fridge. It was taught the rules of chess and could figure out the next best move by crunching 200 million options a second.
research.source: IBM's own history of Deep Blue: the machine evaluated 200 million chess positions per second.

reckons.claim: Nobody actually knows why nerds love chess. But there's some reasonable stuff we can assume.

research.quote: They called it the 'Mechanical Turk'. Built by a Hungarian showman to impress an Austrian Empress.
research.source: IEEE Spectrum on Wolfgang von Kempelen's chess automaton, built in 1770 for Empress Maria Theresa.

research.quote: So he was very disappointed to be beaten by a robot.
research.source: Benjamin Franklin played the Turk in Paris in 1783 and lost. The disappointment is our guess — the game is on record at the US National Archives' Founders Online.

research.quote: The Turk went on tour for over 80 years and wiped the floor with the smartest players in town.
research.source: IEEE Spectrum: the Turk toured Europe and America from 1770 until it was destroyed by fire in 1854, beating most challengers.

research.quote: One was a math nerd called Charles Babbage. He couldn't work out how the robot won.
research.source: IEEE Spectrum: Babbage played the Turk in 1819, lost, and suspected a trick without solving it.

reckons.claim: We've kept the big numbers deliberately loose. Nobody hand counted all the books in all the libraries.

research.quote: Then came the big unlock from Google. In 2017, a small team of researchers were after better ways to do translation.
research.source: “Attention Is All You Need”, the 2017 transformer paper by eight Google researchers, framed around machine translation.

research.quote: It's also why NVIDIA leapt from graphics-chip king to the top of the big cash leaderboard.
research.source: Al Jazeera, 19 June 2024: NVIDIA became the world's most valuable company, passing Microsoft.

research.quote: Data was named the new oil.
research.source: The UK Information Commissioner's Office attributes “data is the new oil” to mathematician Clive Humby in 2006.

reckons.claim: We know who was there and what happened next. We're guessing at what they were thinking at the time.

research.quote: It wasn't exactly a pub, it was the Rosewood Sand Hill in Silicon Valley.
research.source: Fortune's account of the July 2015 dinner at the Rosewood Sand Hill on Menlo Park's Sand Hill Road where OpenAI was hatched.

research.quote: After winning a famous picture-guessing competition, everyone spotted the potential of what they'd invented.
research.source: The AlexNet paper by Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton, which won the 2012 ImageNet image-recognition challenge.

research.quote: And before you could say stock options, Hinton's lab was gobbled by Google for a very big cheque.
research.source: CBC News, March 2013: Google acquired Hinton's University of Toronto startup DNNresearch. The price wasn't disclosed.

research.quote: So Google got out its chequebook again and paid over ten times more to lock down the promising tech.
research.source: TechCrunch, January 2014: Google bought DeepMind for a reported $500 million or more — more than ten times the roughly $44 million reported for DNNresearch.

research.quote: Together with Altman and crew, they conceived the idea of OpenAI.
research.source: Fortune's account of OpenAI's founding, from the 2015 dinner through launch.

research.quote: just before Christmas in 2015, OpenAI was launched.
research.source: Fast Company: OpenAI announced itself on December 11, 2015.

research.quote: Over a billion dollars was pledged to launch the lab. With all the usual suspects promising cash in the tin. Although not all that much of it ever showed up.
research.source: OpenAI's own account: $1 billion was pledged at launch; Musk contributed less than $45 million and other donors over $90 million.

research.quote: They couldn't very well accept money from Google. So they chose Microsoft instead.
research.source: Fortune on Microsoft's investment in OpenAI, starting with $1 billion in 2019.

research.quote: Most famous was Dario Amodei. He was poached from Google to help build GPT-3.
research.source: Dario Amodei's own biography: left Google for OpenAI in 2016, where he led the teams behind GPT-2 and GPT-3.

research.quote: When that was apparently not the plan he gathered a team to set up Anthropic.
research.source: Anthropic's own announcement, 2021: founded by Dario Amodei with former OpenAI colleagues.

research.quote: He joined a coup in 2023 that had Altman fired for at least a weekend.
research.source: ABC News: Altman was fired on Friday November 17, 2023, with Sutskever on the board that removed him, and was reinstated within five days.

research.quote: He went on to set up Safe Superintelligence.
research.source: Safe Superintelligence Inc., co-founded by Ilya Sutskever in June 2024, in the company's own words.

research.quote: Musk threw a spat when he couldn't be the boss. He cut off the cash and crossed the road to build a toy of his own.
research.source: OpenAI's own account of Musk's 2018 departure, the funding he withheld, and his move to build a competitor.

research.quote: He hung in for a while, won a Nobel Prize.
research.source: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2024, awarded to Geoffrey Hinton and John Hopfield.

reckons.claim: This tech changes all the time. Top line, the robots are more similar than different. But they'll all tell you they're special in their own way.
Whether or not the robots think is more philosophy than science. Our take is that memory and math doesn't make them Plato.

research.quote: Plenty of lawyers have tuned up their arguments with a robot. Many go on to cite cases that don't exist.
research.source: Mata v. Avianca: the June 2023 federal court opinion sanctioning lawyers who filed ChatGPT-invented cases.

research.quote: One measure of success is the number of things a robot can do in a row. That doubles every year. And then some.
research.source: METR's research on task length: the length of tasks AI can complete has been doubling about every seven months.

reckons.claim: Token economics is a moving target. This is more about how tokens work than where the money will land.
'Better chats beat better prompts' is an opinion based on experience. You'll easily find people who believe just the opposite.

research.quote: 'Prompt engineer' was the hottest job of 2023. Salaries went nuts
research.source: Fortune, March 2023, on prompt-engineering roles advertising salaries up to $335,000.

reckons.claim: We reckon training is the big unlock. Because it usually is.

research.quote: More than a billion people now chat with a bot on the regular.
research.source: CNBC, June 2026: ChatGPT alone passed one billion monthly mobile app users, per Sensor Tower.

reckons.claim: The basics of how to customise robots are sound. The language will likely bounce around, bot by bot over time.
Nobody knows what tomorrow will throw. But we do know what's less likely. So we've stacked the doom in order from catastrophe to creeper.

research.quote: They're also twenty times more likely to kill you than a shark.
research.source: The US CDC counted about 22 cattle-related deaths a year; shark attacks kill about one American a year. The twenty-times is that arithmetic.

research.quote: That's roughly the plot of 2001: A Space Odyssey. Stanley Kubrick's HAL was scary in 1968.
research.source: The American Film Institute's catalogue entry for 2001: A Space Odyssey, released April 1968.

research.quote: An Oxford academic wrote a paper on the risks of superintelligence. A thought experiment with stationery.
research.source: Nick Bostrom's 2003 paper “Ethical Issues in Advanced Artificial Intelligence”, with the paperclip thought experiment, on his own site.

research.quote: The AI Safety Index grades the big labs. But the best they could score in the first few years was C+.
research.source: The Future of Life Institute's AI Safety Index: C+ has been the top overall grade across its editions, including Summer 2026.

research.quote: Even experts studying deepfakes only pick them half the time.
research.source: A 2024 meta-analysis of 56 deepfake-detection studies found people spot good deepfakes at about chance — roughly half the time.

reckons.claim: Workslop is a term coined by management consultants and is now widely uttered as an under-breath expletive.
Our big assumption is that history repeats. We don't know that it will. It just always has before.

research.quote: From 25 million in 1920, they started a gentle downhill trot. By 1965, only 3 million were left.
research.source: US equine census figures: about 25.2 million horses and mules in 1920, about 3.1 million at the last count in 1960.

research.quote: One US crowd who counts layoffs for a living keeps a running tally on AI-related job cuts.
research.source: Challenger, Gray & Christmas, whose layoff reports have tracked job cuts attributed to AI since 2023.

research.quote: In a stadium packed with 50,000 workers, only 22 were told that a robot took their job. Less a revolution. More a bathroom break.
research.source: The stadium is our maths: Challenger counted 71,825 announced job cuts naming AI across 2023–2025, out of roughly 163 million US jobs — about 22 in every 50,000.

research.quote: Unemployment (in rich countries) stubbornly hovers around 5%.
research.source: OECD figures, June 2026: unemployment across member countries at 5.0%, near that level for a fifth year.

research.quote: Back in the 1900s, 40% of Americans worked on farms. Today it's less than 2%.
research.source: The US Department of Agriculture: farm jobs were 41% of the workforce in 1900 and under 2% by 2000.

research.quote: Over half the jobs we do today didn't exist when they were starting out.
research.source: Research by MIT economist David Autor and colleagues: about 60% of 2018 US jobs were in kinds of work that didn't exist in 1940.

reckons.claim: Agents are usually smarter than puppies. The watch out is supervision, not intelligence.
It's true that robots do what they do by stealing. So the question we're really asking is who's committing the crime.

research.quote: Rather than hand it over, he kept it and he tinkered with it for sixteen years.
research.source: Time's account of the Mona Lisa: begun in Florence in 1503, still with Leonardo in France at his death in 1519.

research.quote: Then it was stolen. Story turned to legend and that enigmatic smile became one of the most widely shared images in the world.
research.source: PBS on the 1911 Louvre theft, which turned a little-known portrait into a household name.

research.quote: For one crazy year in 2021 the NFT market boomed to $25B before crashing
research.source: DappRadar's 2021 industry report counted $23 billion in NFT sales — we rounded up with the crowd.

research.quote: MTV launched in 1981. And boldly played that Buggles track as first cab off the rank.
research.source: Rolling Stone: MTV went to air on August 1, 1981, opening with “Video Killed the Radio Star”.

research.quote: Streaming killed MTV by 2025. And yes, they had the Buggles play it out.
research.source: NME: MTV's music-only channels shut down on December 31, 2025, closing with the same Buggles video they opened with.

research.quote: From the moment streaming started, vinyl came back from the dead. Sales shot up year on year.
research.source: The Recording Industry Association of America: 2025 was vinyl's 19th straight year of growth.

reckons.claim: Nobody knows why the em-dash became a thing. But people like to know why odd stuff happens. So we've given it a go with guesswork.
We cherry picked three stories to make a point. History is never that tidy. Plus robots having original ideas is about how you define 'original'.

research.quote: Fleming noticed that mould was attacking his experiment. It killed some bacteria growing in the dish.
research.source: The American Chemical Society's history of penicillin: Fleming's 1928 observation of mould killing bacteria in a petri dish.

research.quote: He made a discovery in an untidy lab, but it took ten years and a stack of experiments to turn that discovery into drugs.
research.source: The American Chemical Society: penicillin stayed a laboratory curiosity for the next decade, until Florey and Chain's team turned it into a drug in the 1940s.

research.quote: Mortality rates dropped dramatically. This bold new idea of doctors washing with decent soap could actually save lives.
research.source: The Linda Hall Library on Semmelweis: death rates in his Vienna clinic ran over 13% against 2% in the midwives' clinic, and fell once handwashing came in.

research.quote: In the end they quietly had him committed.
research.source: The Linda Hall Library: Semmelweis was committed to an asylum, where he died in 1865.

research.quote: Demis Hassabis is a video game designer. He started DeepMind
research.source: Hassabis's own biography at Isomorphic Labs: designed the game Theme Park at 17, founded DeepMind in 2010.

research.quote: Scientists had been working on it since the 60s. Thousands of biologists, fifty-odd years, building, testing, authenticating, one fold at a time.
research.source: The Nobel Committee called protein-structure prediction a 50-year-old problem when it awarded the 2024 Chemistry prize.

research.quote: There are more possible shapes than atoms in the universe.
research.source: The classic framing of Levinthal's paradox: a protein's possible folds outnumber astronomical figures, popularised by DeepMind as more than the atoms in the universe.

research.quote: In 2022 they released the predicted shapes of over 200 million proteins. Pretty much the known protein universe, free and publicly available
research.source: DeepMind's own announcement, July 2022: predicted structures for over 200 million proteins, free for anyone.

research.quote: That's a starting point for brand new drugs, nailed by a robot and recognised with a Nobel Prize.
research.source: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024, awarded to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for protein-structure prediction.

research.quote: Genius, according to Edison, is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration.
research.source: Quote Investigator's provenance record: attributed to Edison from around 1902, first printed in Harper's Monthly in 1932.

reckons.claim: Ethics needs another twenty books. We haven't done it justice. The basic idea is write the rules before you play the game.

research.quote: Like that doctor in 2018 who was aiming to help kids at risk of HIV. He edited their genes to make them immune.
research.source: Science on He Jiankui, who announced in November 2018 that he had edited embryos aiming to confer resistance to HIV.

research.quote: It's a fine line between a Nobel Prize and prison. He won the latter.
research.source: Science: He Jiankui was sentenced to three years in jail in December 2019.

research.quote: Tech is already implanted into brains.
research.source: Neuralink's own update: its first human brain-computer implant was carried out in January 2024.

reckons.claim: Again we've based the fortune telling on the clues we get from history. Past returns aren't proof of future performance.

research.quote: Right across town we'd already invented much smaller motors that could do a better job. But it took over 30 years to bring them in.
research.source: Economic historian Paul David's “The Dynamo and the Computer”, 1990: factories took decades to redesign around the electric motor.

reckons.claim: The idea that people don't change is evolutionary jazz hands. Individuals change all the time. As a species, we just left the cave.
All the previous assumptions wrapped into a promise that's really a guess. But the big point is that the robots are here. Let's play.
